model_output.score_comment_short: The ICU duties are specific, though charge and teaching work need more detail.
model_output.score_comment_long: The current role names patient load, critical care therapies, and charge-nurse frequency. The precepting and committee entries say less about what you contributed. Adding a concrete responsibility to each would make those parts easier to assess.
model_output.score_plain: Your clinical setting and patient-care responsibilities are easy to place for nursing roles. A reviewer may still want a fuller picture of your charge and teaching duties.
model_output.first_impression: Your current role is clearly centered on medical ICU care, including ventilators and continuous renal replacement therapy. Charge, precepting, and committee work also appear, but receive much less space.
model_output.biggest_gap_example: "Member of the unit's sepsis bundle compliance committee" identifies the group but not your contribution, leaving a reviewer unsure what you did there.
model_output.summary: Caring for 2 critically ill patients per shift in a 24-bed medical ICU gives a reviewer useful context for your current bedside role. Your work also spans charge coverage and orientation of new graduates, alongside earlier telemetry care. The resume presents an established staff nurse with added unit responsibilities. It does not yet explain what you handle as charge nurse, which makes that part of your role difficult to compare with other charge assignments.
strengths: The combination of ventilated patients, vasoactive drips, and continuous renal replacement therapy names the care you manage rather than relying on an ICU title alone.
Arizona multistate compact licensure and CCRN are easy to find near the top.
The telemetry role specifies 4 to 5 patients per shift and includes post-cardiac catheterization care, making the earlier bedside work concrete.
gaps: The orientation entry does not describe how you supported new graduates, so your teaching role is difficult to distinguish from a brief assignment.
The rapid response entry does not say what you did as part of the floor team, limiting the picture of your contribution during those calls.
Discharge education names medications but not the questions or needs you addressed with patients and families.
